finding: The faith-and-deeds pair is explicitly joined to a promise that no good worker’s reward is wasted, giving the focus’s escape from loss a concrete counterpart.

evidence.ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ إِنَّا لَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ مَنْ أَحْسَنَ عَمَلًا

activation: The shared opening predicates meet the focus’s verdict of human loss; 18:30 answers with non-wasted reward.
limits: 18:30 does not include mutual counsel to truth or patience, and its promise concerns reward.

finding: The warning that Musa cannot be patient “with me” places ṣabr in a teacher–student relation: endurance is tested while staying with someone through instruction.

evidence.ar: وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ
إِنَّكَ لَن تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِىَ صَبْرًۭا

activation: The focus’s final charge names ṣabr; this episode makes endurance relational by specifying “with me.”
limits: The relation here is between one teacher and one learner, not mutual counsel among a group; the verse does not mention truth.

finding: Here patience is tested against what Musa has not yet comprehended, so endurance accompanies a gap in knowledge before events can be understood.

evidence.ar: وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ
وَكَيْفَ تَصْبِرُ عَلَىٰ مَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِۦ خُبْرًۭا

activation: The focus pairs truth with patience; the question links patience to an account not yet grasped.
limits: This does not make patience passive acceptance or say that the focus’s truth is hidden knowledge.

finding: Musa promises to be patient if God wills and couples that promise with not disobeying the guide, depicting ṣabr as disciplined following.

evidence.ar: وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ
سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ صَابِرًۭا وَلَآ أَعْصِى لَكَ أَمْرًۭا

activation: The focus’s patience charge is followed here by a pledge linking endurance to obedience during the journey.
limits: Musa makes an individual pledge; this is not reciprocal exhortation.

finding: The episode closes by naming Musa’s inability to be patient as the matter now given its explanation; the narrative makes patience a demand during the interval before interpretation arrives.

evidence.ar: وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ
ذَٰلِكَ تَأْوِيلُ مَا لَمْ تَسْطِع عَّلَيْهِ صَبْرًۭا

activation: The paired charge to truth and patience can be heard beside a story where explanation comes after patience has been strained.
limits: This episode’s hidden actions and eventual explanation do not define the focus’s truth or identify its community with Musa and his guide.

finding: Another conditional joins belief with righteous action and promises the good reward, reinforcing that this pair can mark a rewarded group while leaving the focus’s communal predicates unspoken.

evidence.ar: ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ
وَأَمَّا مَنْ ءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا فَلَهُۥ جَزَآءً ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ

activation: The focus begins its exception with the same belief-and-action pairing.
limits: 18:88 uses a singular indefinite adjective and says nothing about mutual counsel.

finding: After a warning about those who disbelieved and mocked the signs, believers who do righteous deeds are promised Firdaws; the paired predicates stand opposite mockery in this scene.

evidence.ar: ذَٰلِكَ جَزَآؤُهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ بِمَا كَفَرُوا۟ وَٱتَّخَذُوٓا۟ ءَايَٰتِى وَرُسُلِى هُزُوًا
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ كَانَتْ لَهُمْ جَنَّٰتُ ٱلْفِرْدَوْسِ نُزُلًا

activation: The focus’s opening predicates recur here with a sharply different outcome from disbelief and mockery.
limits: This pairing does not extend to truth and patience in the cited verses.

finding: The surah ends by directing one who hopes to meet the Lord to do “a righteous deed” and avoid associating anyone in worship; the singular indefinite deed differs in form from the focus’s definite plural class of deeds.

evidence.ar: وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ
فَمَن كَانَ يَرْجُوا۟ لِقَآءَ رَبِّهِۦ فَلْيَعْمَلْ عَمَلًۭا صَٰلِحًۭا وَلَا يُشْرِكْ بِعِبَادَةِ رَبِّهِۦٓ أَحَدًۢا

activation: Both passages connect right action with faith in God, while this closing instruction states hope for meeting the Lord as its immediate motive.
limits: The focus itself does not state that motive, and 18:110 does not name mutual counsel.

finding: أَوْصَانِي shares the وصي root with تَوَاصَوْا but uses a different form: Isa receives a charge concerning prayer and zakat for as long as he lives, while the focus makes charging one another reciprocal.

evidence.ar: وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ
وَأَوْصَٰنِى بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱلزَّكَوٰةِ مَا دُمْتُ حَيًّۭا

activation: The repeated tawaṣaw clauses invite comparison with this explicit divine charge and its bāʾ-governed content.
limits: The focus describes mutual human charging; 19:31 describes a charge received by Isa and names different content.

finding: After a generation is described as neglecting prayer and following desires, an exception is made for those who repent, believe, and do right; this is a repair path out of a preceding communal failure.

evidence.ar: فَخَلَفَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِمْ خَلْفٌ أَضَاعُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَٱتَّبَعُوا۟ ٱلشَّهَوَٰتِ
إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ
إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا

activation: Both passages use an exception followed by belief and righteous action; the surrounding verses in Maryam supply a specific prior failure and repair.
limits: Maryam adds repentance and a promise of entry to the Garden, but not mutual exhortation to truth and patience.

finding: The phrase الباقيات الصالحات describes righteous deeds as abiding; beside the focus’s oath by time and verdict of loss, it gives the deeds a contrasting horizon of endurance.

evidence.ar: وَٱلْعَصْرِ
إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ
وَٱلْبَٰقِيَٰتُ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ خَيْرٌ عِندَ رَبِّكَ ثَوَابًۭا وَخَيْرٌۭ مَّرَدًّا

activation: The shared الصالحات wording meets the focus’s time-and-loss frame, while Maryam explicitly calls these deeds abiding.
limits: Maryam does not say that the focus’s deeds are everlasting or identify which deeds it means.

finding: The same faith-and-righteous-deeds formula is followed here by God-given affection, a social outcome that complements the focus’s move from individual predicates to reciprocal communal practice.

evidence.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ سَيَجْعَلُ لَهُمُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ وُدًّۭا

activation: The focus defines a group through shared belief, action, and mutual exhortation; Maryam attaches affection to its first two predicates.
limits: 19:96 attributes affection to God’s making and does not say it results from mutual exhortation.

finding: After the warning that whoever is overtaken by wrath has fallen, God names repentance, belief, righteous action, and then guidance as a path to forgiveness; the sequence answers a fall with return and direction.

evidence.ar: وَمَن يَحْلِلْ عَلَيْهِ غَضَبِى فَقَدْ هَوَىٰ
وَإِنِّى لَغَفَّارٌۭ لِّمَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا ثُمَّ ٱهْتَدَىٰ
إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ

activation: The fall and forgiveness sequence resonates with the focus’s loss verdict and its exception through faith and action.
limits: This verse adds repentance and subsequent guidance; it does not mention the focus’s two mutual charges.

finding: A believer who does righteous deeds is promised neither fear of injustice nor loss of due. The pairing directly counters the failure and wrong named in the preceding verse.

evidence.ar: وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ حَمَلَ ظُلْمًۭا
ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ
وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌۭ فَلَا يَخَافُ ظُلْمًۭا وَلَا هَضْمًۭا

activation: The focus names the same two qualifications; Ṭā Hā places them against failure and guarantees freedom from wrong or deprivation.
limits: The order is reversed, and these verses do not include reciprocal counsel to truth or patience.

finding: One person is told to command his household to pray and to persevere in prayer, a directed household practice that can be compared with the focus’s reciprocal charging to patience.

evidence.ar: وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ
وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱصْطَبِرْ عَلَيْهَا

activation: Both passages join communal or household religious practice with ṣabr; the imperative here specifies the household and prayer.
limits: Ṭā Hā gives a one-way command and personal perseverance, not mutual exhortation; its object is prayer, not patience itself.

finding: Prophetic leaders are described as guided by God’s command and devoted to good works, prayer, and zakat, giving some concrete practices that may fall under the focus’s righteous deeds.

evidence.ar: وَكُلًّۭا جَعَلْنَا صَٰلِحِينَ
يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِمْ فِعْلَ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَإِقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَإِيتَآءَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةِ

activation: The focus’s righteous deeds are the point of comparison; these neighboring verses join righteous status to named communal practices.
limits: This does not enumerate all righteous deeds or include reciprocal counsel to truth and patience.

finding: The named prophets are called patient, then immediately described as among the righteous; patience and righteous standing thus converge in the same people.

evidence.ar: وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ
وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ
كُلٌّۭ مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
إِنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

activation: The focus places righteous deeds and patience together; these adjacent verses apply the corresponding qualities to one prophetic group.
limits: The verses classify these people but do not say their patience was mutually advised or specify their deeds.

finding: The response to Zakariyya’s prayer is followed by a description of the family hastening to good works and calling on God in hope and fear, adding urgency and supplication to the action profile.

evidence.ar: رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْنِى فَرْدًۭا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلْوَٰرِثِينَ
إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ يُسَٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَيَدْعُونَنَا رَغَبًۭا وَرَهَبًۭا

activation: The focus’s action condition is echoed by a plural household characterized through hastening toward good.
limits: The passage does not use الصالحات or mention mutual exhortation, truth, or patience.

finding: A believer’s righteous effort is neither denied nor lost: it is recorded. This gives a direct assurance against the focus’s loss verdict.

evidence.ar: إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ
ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ
فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌۭ فَلَا كُفْرَانَ لِسَعْيِهِۦ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ كَٰتِبُونَ

activation: The shared believer-and-deeds condition is followed here by assurance that the effort will be recognized and recorded.
limits: The verse focuses on an individual’s effort and does not include the focus’s mutual counsel predicates.

finding: The worshippers are described as patient under affliction, establishing prayer, and spending from their provision; this offers examples of steadfastness alongside enacted good.

evidence.ar: وَٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَصَابَهُمْ وَٱلْمُقِيمِى ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَٰهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ

activation: The focus’s ṣabr and righteous-action clauses meet this list of patience and devotional practice.
limits: The list does not say these people urge one another, and the verse does not call these specific actions الصالحات.

finding: Faith and righteous deeds again appear together with forgiveness and generous provision; the verse confirms the pairing while offering no counterpart to the focus’s reciprocal clauses.

evidence.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ
فَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌۭ وَرِزْقٌۭ كَرِيمٌۭ

activation: The same two predicates open the focus’s exception and define those promised these gifts.
limits: The verse says nothing about truth, patience, or mutual practice.

finding: Believers are commanded to worship and do good so that they may prosper; the following address expands this into striving, witness, prayer, and zakat. Prosperity supplies a positive outcome against the focus’s loss verdict.

evidence.ar: إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ
يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱرْكَعُوا۟ وَٱسْجُدُوا۟ وَٱعْبُدُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ وَٱفْعَلُوا۟ ٱلْخَيْرَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ
لِيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ شَهِيدًا عَلَيْكُمْ وَتَكُونُوا۟ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ ۚ فَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ

activation: The addressed believers and imperative good works resonate with the focus’s exception; تُفْلِحُونَ names the contrasting outcome.
limits: The passage does not say that prosperity comes through mutual counsel to truth and patience, and its listed practices are not exhaustive.

finding: Guarding trusts and covenants gives the faithful profile a relational accountability dimension that can sit beside the focus’s shared charge to uphold truth.

evidence.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَمَٰنَٰتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ رَٰعُونَ

activation: The focus’s truth charge is addressed to a group; this verse specifies faithful conduct toward trusts and covenants.
limits: It does not use الحق or وصى, so the relation is social and ethical rather than a wording parallel.

finding: The messengers are told to consume what is good and act righteously, then reminded that God knows their deeds; the next verse calls their community one.

evidence.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلرُّسُلُ كُلُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ وَٱعْمَلُوا۟ صَٰلِحًا ۖ إِنِّى بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ عَلِيمٌۭ
وَإِنَّ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ

activation: The focus’s righteous-action condition is addressed here to messengers within an explicitly united community.
limits: This passage does not mention patience or mutual exhortation, and its singular صَالِحًا differs from the focus’s plural noun.

finding: At death, a person asks to return so he can do righteous work, but is refused and faces a barrier until resurrection; it dramatizes the time-bound urgency behind the focus’s active deeds.

evidence.ar: وَٱلْعَصْرِ
وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ
قَالَ رَبِّ ٱرْجِعُونِ
لَعَلِّىٓ أَعْمَلُ صَٰلِحًۭا فِيمَا تَرَكْتُ ۚ كَلَّآ ۚ إِنَّهَا كَلِمَةٌ هُوَ قَآئِلُهَا ۖ وَمِن وَرَآئِهِم بَرْزَخٌ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ

activation: The focus opens with an oath by time and requires deeds; this scene shows a request for those deeds after life has ended.
limits: The passage does not specify the focus’s other three conditions or say what deeds the speaker intended.

finding: Those mocked by their opponents are rewarded for their patience and declared the ones who succeed; this casts ṣabr as endurance under social ridicule with a victorious outcome.

evidence.ar: فَٱتَّخَذْتُمُوهُمْ سِخْرِيًّا حَتَّىٰٓ أَنسَوْكُمْ ذِكْرِى وَكُنتُم مِّنْهُمْ تَضْحَكُونَ
وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ
إِنِّى جَزَيْتُهُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ بِمَا صَبَرُوٓا۟ أَنَّهُمْ هُمُ ٱلْفَآئِزُونَ

activation: The focus’s patience clause meets an account of mockery answered by patient endurance and success.
limits: The verse says they were patient but does not depict them advising one another to be so.

finding: After the rule against false accusers, an exception for those who repent and reform restores their standing; exception and repair answer condemnation in a way comparable to the focus’s exception from loss.

evidence.ar: وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْفَٰسِقُونَ
إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ
إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ تَابُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ وَأَصْلَحُوا۟

activation: Both verses use إِلَّا to mark an exit from a preceding judgment; the shared صلح root links reform here to the focus’s righteous deeds.
limits: Here the form is a verb of reform after a particular offense, not the focus’s noun for righteous deeds; it says nothing about mutual counsel.

finding: In response to a wrong, believers are told to keep aiding vulnerable people, forgive, and pardon; this could specify how patience and truthful communal repair operate after injury.

evidence.ar: وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ
وَلَا يَأْتَلِ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْفَضْلِ مِنكُمْ وَٱلسَّعَةِ أَن يُؤْتُوٓا۟ أُو۟لِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَٱلْمَسَٰكِينَ وَٱلْمُهَٰجِرِينَ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَلْيَعْفُوا۟ وَلْيَصْفَحُوٓا۟

missing: These verses do not explicitly connect forgiveness or continued aid to the focus’s sabr or haqq; another ayah linking ṣabr to pardon after harm, or a lexical account of ṣabr’s scope, could establish the connection.

finding: The phrase بِٱلْحَقِّ also describes God’s answer to opponents’ examples, followed by the best explanation; in al-Furqan, truth is the revealed reply to polemic.

evidence.ar: وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلْحَقِّ
وَلَا يَأْتُونَكَ بِمَثَلٍ إِلَّا جِئْنَٰكَ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَأَحْسَنَ تَفْسِيرًا

activation: The exact bāʾ-governed phrase recurs, while the surrounding words specify an argumentative setting for haqq.
limits: In 25:33 God brings the answer to the Prophet; it is not mutual human exhortation as in the focus.

finding: When ignorant people address them, the servants of the Merciful answer with peace; this is a concrete social response compatible with patient restraint under provocation.

evidence.ar: وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ
وَعِبَادُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ هَوْنًۭا وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ ٱلْجَٰهِلُونَ قَالُوا۟ سَلَٰمًۭا

activation: The focus makes patience a shared charge; this plural portrait shows how its addressees respond when confronted by ignorant speech.
limits: The verse does not use صبر or say that silence and peaceful speech exhaust its meaning.

finding: Measured spending, avoiding both extravagance and stinginess, gives a concrete example of balanced conduct in the portrait of the servants of the Merciful.

evidence.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَنفَقُوا۟ لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا۟ وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا۟ وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ قَوَامًۭا

activation: The focus’s broad righteous-deeds condition can encompass this carefully balanced action.
limits: The verse does not identify the spending as an instance of الصالحات or mention truth and patience.

finding: After grave wrongdoing, an exception joins repentance, belief, and righteous action to God’s transformation of bad deeds into good ones; the exit from ruin can involve reversal, not simply avoidance of punishment.

evidence.ar: يُضَٰعَفْ لَهُ ٱلْعَذَابُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ
إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ
إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلًۭا صَٰلِحًۭا فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمْ حَسَنَٰتٍۢ

activation: The shared exception and belief/action pair are placed here after specified serious wrongs, with an outcome of transformation.
limits: The focus does not specify repentance, prior crimes, or transformation of bad deeds into good.

finding: The next verse restates repentance and righteous action as a return to God, making return itself the continuing movement after the exception in 25:70.

evidence.ar: إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلًۭا صَٰلِحًۭا
وَمَن تَابَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا فَإِنَّهُۥ يَتُوبُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَتَابًۭا

activation: The focus presents deeds as part of the way out of loss; al-Furqan continues that path by naming the deed-maker’s return to God.
limits: The verse omits belief and does not describe mutual counsel or the outcome of the return.

finding: The servants refuse false witness and pass vain speech with dignity, joining truthfulness in public speech to restrained conduct around empty talk.

evidence.ar: وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ
وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَشْهَدُونَ ٱلزُّورَ وَإِذَا مَرُّوا۟ بِٱللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا۟ كِرَامًۭا

activation: The focus pairs haqq with ṣabr; this portrait gives distinct social behaviors that bear on truth and restraint.
limits: 25:72 does not use either focus noun or say that these behaviors are the precise meaning of its two charges.

finding: Abraham asks to be joined to the righteous and for a truthful remembrance among later generations; the passage gives righteous standing an intergenerational horizon.

evidence.ar: وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلْحَقِّ
رَبِّ هَبْ لِى حُكْمًۭا وَأَلْحِقْنِى بِٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
وَٱجْعَل لِّى لِسَانَ صِدْقٍۢ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ

activation: The focus binds a group to truth and righteous action; Abraham’s prayer joins righteous company to truthful mention in later generations.
limits: This is a prayer for status and remembrance, not a description of mutual exhortation or a claim that the focus guarantees posthumous reputation.

finding: Ṣāliḥ here is the prophet’s proper name, not evidence by itself about the focus’s الصالحات; the relevant scene is his one-way admonition, “ألا تتقون,” compared with the focus’s mutual exhortation.

evidence.ar: إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ صَٰلِحٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ

activation: The shared feature is communal exhortation: a messenger addresses his people, while the focus describes believers charging one another.
limits: The address is a call to fear God, not explicit counsel to truth and patience; the proper name should not be treated as a lexical occurrence of the focus’s deed class.

finding: A group is defined by corruption in the land and failure to reform, a direct social antithesis to righteous deeds; the surrounding command not to obey them sharpens the contrast.

evidence.ar: وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ
وَلَا تُطِيعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ
ٱلَّذِينَ يُفْسِدُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا يُصْلِحُونَ

activation: The focus’s ṣāliḥāt and the paired negative description share the صلح root while assigning opposing social roles.
limits: The description concerns a specific group in the Thamud narrative and does not spell out the focus’s positive practices.

finding: This is a close exception parallel: after poets are faulted for saying what they do not do, the exception names believers who act righteously, remember God, and answer after being wronged. Deeds, truthful integrity, and response to injustice converge here.

evidence.ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ
وَأَنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ مَا لَا يَفْعَلُونَ
إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَذَكَرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرًۭا وَٱنتَصَرُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا ظُلِمُوا۟

activation: The exception and its first two predicates match the focus closely; the preceding charge about speech without action brings truthfulness into view, and the final clause follows wrong suffered.
limits: This passage specifies remembrance and answering after oppression, not the focus’s exact reciprocal practices of truth and patience.

finding: After the ant warns its people, Solomon asks God to enable gratitude and a pleasing righteous deed, then asks to be admitted among righteous servants; good action is framed as a response to received favor.

evidence.ar: قَالَتْ نَمْلَةٌۭ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّمْلُ ٱدْخُلُوا۟ مَسَٰكِنَكُمْ لَا يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ سُلَيْمَٰنُ وَجُنُودُهُۥ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِىٓ أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَىَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَىَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صَٰلِحًۭا تَرْضَىٰهُ وَأَدْخِلْنِى بِرَحْمَتِكَ فِى عِبَادِكَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

activation: The scene moves from concern for vulnerable creatures to a prayer for grateful and pleasing action, touching the focus’s deed condition.
limits: Solomon’s individual prayer does not describe mutual exhortation or patient response to harm.

finding: The nine men are labeled corruptors who do not reform, then immediately plot murder and plan a false oath. Their coordinated deception is a sharp counter-image to a community defined by righteous work and mutual truth.

evidence.ar: وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلْحَقِّ
وَكَانَ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ تِسْعَةُ رَهْطٍۢ يُفْسِدُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا يُصْلِحُونَ
تَقَاسَمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُۥ وَأَهْلَهُۥ ثُمَّ لَنَقُولَنَّ لِوَلِيِّهِۦ مَا شَهِدْنَا مَهْلِكَ أَهْلِهِۦ وَإِنَّا لَصَٰدِقُونَ

activation: The focus’s truth-bearing mutual practice contrasts with a group whose corruption leads into conspiracy and a planned falsehood.
limits: The verses narrate one faction’s scheme; they do not directly define the focus’s communal group or prescribe its response.

finding: Musa’s opponent calls his action tyranny and asks whether he intends to be among the reformers; the next verse gives Musa a warning from a well-wisher. This raises whether righteous action is tested by restraint and truthful counsel when intervention risks force.

evidence.ar: وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلْحَقِّ
إِن تُرِيدُ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ جَبَّارًۭا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا تُرِيدُ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُصْلِحِينَ
إِنِّى لَكَ مِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ

missing: The accusation is spoken by an involved person, and these verses do not establish whether it accurately judges Musa’s act. The following narrative outcome or an explicit divine assessment could decide whether this is a test of reforming action and truthful advice.

finding: The proposed employer describes the strong, trustworthy hire, offers a measured term, and expects to be among the righteous; the scene gives righteous identity a setting of work and fair dealing.

evidence.ar: إِنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ ٱسْتَـْٔجَرْتَ ٱلْقَوِىُّ ٱلْأَمِينُ
وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشُقَّ عَلَيْكَ ۚ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

activation: The focus’s righteous deeds are compared with a narrative where ṣāliḥīn describes expected character in an employment agreement.
limits: This is a personal assurance about character and fairness, not a communal set of deeds or mutual counsel.

finding: After people cannot answer questions about their former associations, another path is stated: whoever repents, believes, and acts righteously may be among those who prosper.

evidence.ar: فَعَمِيَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْأَنۢبَآءُ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ فَهُمْ لَا يَتَسَآءَلُونَ
فَأَمَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا فَعَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُفْلِحِينَ

activation: The focus’s exit from loss through belief and deeds is echoed in a passage that attaches repentance and action to possible flourishing.
limits: The verse gives an individual alternative and omits mutual exhortation; the outcome is expressed as hope, فَعَسَىٰ.

finding: Those given knowledge urge people dazzled by Qarun’s display to value God’s reward for believers who act righteously, then associate that reward with patience. The passage shows patience resisting the pull of worldly display.

evidence.ar: ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ
وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ
قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُرِيدُونَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا يَٰلَيْتَ لَنَا مِثْلَ مَآ أُوتِىَ قَٰرُونُ
ثَوَابُ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌۭ لِّمَنْ ءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا وَلَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلصَّٰبِرُونَ

activation: The passage brings belief, righteous action, and patience into one scene where people are being counseled away from worldly envy.
limits: It does not name haqq or state that ṣabr is mutually advised; the referent of ـهَا in يُلَقَّىٰهَا is not explicit in the excerpt.
